title: Create Internal Certifications for Team Members to Showcase Their Skills
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece encourages leaders to build internal certification programs for roles that lack an external accrediting body, arguing these homegrown credentials can carry as much value and credibility as industry certifications. The recommended process starts by having recognized masters of a role identify the core skills, experiences, and acumen that define high competence, then building a demonstration and measurement process around them. Beyond signaling proficiency to the organization, the article frames certification as a source of personal pride and motivation for the people who earn it, and a useful signal to leaders about who is investing in career growth.
points: Many roles lack an external certifying body, but leaders can create equally credible internal certifications.
The design process starts by having recognized masters of a role define the core skills, experiences, and acumen that constitute competence.
A rigorous, well-designed internal certification becomes both a source of pride and proof of mastery for those who earn it.
Certification participation signals to leaders which team members are most focused on career growth.
quotes: When thoughtfully designed and instilled with rigor, Certifications provide tangible evidence of skill achievement.
The good news is that savvy leaders can create their own , sometimes with even more value than external accreditations.
those who are considered masters in the role can help to identify the core skills and practices that define high competence.
By engaging in the Certification process and attaining its endorsement, they achieve a personal satisfaction that energizes their learning
Oddly enough, Certification creates as much self-recognition as it offers social proof.
